UnitedHealth said the Change Healthcare cyberattack, detected on February 21, 2024, raised its costs, cut Optum Insight revenue and weighed on cash flow. For FY2024 it reported $2.2 billion of direct response costs and $867 million of estimated business disruption impacts. It also provided interest-free loans of more than $9 billion to care providers. Consolidated revenue still rose 7.71% to $400.278 billion. Operating income was nearly flat, down 0.22% to $32.287 billion. Net income fell 35.64% to $14.405 billion, and operating cash flow fell 16.73% to $24.204 billion. The filings do not isolate how much of these consolidated changes came from the attack. Other factors, including Medicare Advantage funding reductions, also weighed on results.
UnitedHealth said it identified on February 21, 2024 that cybercrime threat actors had gained access to certain Change Healthcare IT systems, and it isolated the impacted systems to protect partners and customers. The 10-K describes Change Healthcare as a business it had recently acquired. The data involved contained protected health information or personally identifiable information.
For FY2024 UnitedHealth said it incurred $2.2 billion of direct response costs and provided interest-free loans to care providers of more than $9 billion through December 31, 2024. It also reported estimated Optum Insight business disruption impacts of $867 million, reflecting lost revenue while maintaining full readiness of the affected Change Healthcare services.
At Optum Insight, UnitedHealth said revenues decreased primarily due to business disruption impacts from the cyberattack, partly offset by technology services growth. Earnings from operations decreased primarily due to direct response costs and business disruption impacts.
UnitedHealth also cited incremental medical costs for accommodations to support care providers as a factor in lower UnitedHealthcare earnings from operations. It named this alongside Medicare Advantage funding reductions, Medicaid redeterminations and member mix. In Q1 2024 it said it incurred $340 million of medical costs from temporarily suspending some care management activities. That figure reached $630 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2024.
Consolidated FY2024 revenue was about $400.28 billion, up from $371.62 billion in FY2023, a rise of about 7.71%. Revenue still grew overall despite the Optum Insight disruption.
Operating income was nearly flat: $32.287 billion in FY2024 versus $32.358 billion in FY2023, a change of about -0.22%.
Net income fell about 35.64%, from $22.381 billion in FY2023 to $14.405 billion in FY2024. The Q1 2024 net loss was $1.409 billion. In Q2 2024 UnitedHealth said diluted EPS was impacted by the loss on its South American subsidiaries held for sale and by the cyberattack.
Operating cash flow fell about 16.73%, from $29.068 billion in FY2023 to $24.204 billion in FY2024. UnitedHealth attributed the decrease to CMS Medicare funding reductions, Change Healthcare cyberattack response actions, increased medical costs and changes in working capital accounts. The loans to care providers were a separate use of cash.
UnitedHealth expects to keep incurring direct response costs and business disruption impacts, to a lesser extent, in 2025 as it works to bring transaction volumes back to pre-event levels and win new business. It warned that risks related to impacted data, litigation, reputational harm and regulatory actions could adversely affect its financial condition or results of operations.
